title: Scythian and Saka steppe culture
summary: Scythians were nomadic and semi-nomadic peoples who ruled the Eurasian steppe for much of the first millennium BCE, sharing elements of material culture from the lower Danube to the Yenisei. The Saka of Kazakhstan are placed in the 7th–3rd century BCE, and in Tuva the royal burial monument Arzhan-2 was built in the 7th century BC.

uncertainty.note: Start is the 7th century BC date for the Arzhan-2 monument; end follows the 7th–3rd century BCE span of the Scythian map in the Scientific Reports article. Earlier and later Scythian-style dates exist but were not read on opened pages.
